title: Five Guides for avoiding very beautiful surprises
description: Five recent PatinaHall Guides help buyers check wall systems, beds, pairs, mirrors and stone tops before enthusiasm starts carrying furniture upstairs.
label: Buyer update

paragraphs: Vintage furniture is allowed to have history. It is also allowed to have brackets, non-standard measurements, replaced parts and a complicated relationship with gravity. The surprise should be the object’s story, not the missing wall fitting.
Five recent PatinaHall Guides turn those details into useful questions, measurements and seller requests. They are written to use beside a listing, not to admire from a safe distance.

sections.heading: 1. A wall system: count the parts before counting the shelves
paragraphs: How to buy a vintage wall-mounted shelving system begins with an inventory. Rails, hangers, brackets, shelves, cabinets and loose hardware all get counted before the wall gets involved. Without the right fittings, a wall system can become a distinguished collection of optimistic planks.

sections.heading: 2. A vintage bed: let centimetres settle the argument
paragraphs: How to measure a vintage bed frame for a modern mattress ignores the words double and king until the opening has been measured at several points. Bed-size names travel badly; centimetres have fewer opinions. The Guide keeps the frame, supports, mattress requirements, finished height and delivery route in the same decision.

sections.heading: 3. A pair or set: compare every member
paragraphs: How to compare a vintage pair or set gives every object an identifier, then repeats the same photographs, dimensions, marks and functional checks. Two chairs may be wonderful cousins without being identical twins, and one heroic photograph should not be promoted to spokesperson for the whole family.

sections.heading: 4. A mirror: the useful evidence may be behind you
paragraphs: How to buy a vintage mirror separates the complete object, the useful reflection and the wall it will occupy. Glass, frame, backing, retention, hanging points, weight and route belong to one plan. A flattering reflection is lovely; it is not a condition report.

sections.heading: 5. A marble or stone top: invite gravity to the meeting
paragraphs: How to inspect marble and stone furniture tops follows the surface, edges, underside, support, attachment, dimensions and reported weight before handing treatment and movement to the right specialists. Gravity is an excellent critic and a terrible moving assistant.

sections.heading: A field manual, not a hunt for perfection
paragraphs: These Guides are not instructions for finding flawless furniture. They help decide whether the exact piece, understood condition, likely work and route home are right for the buyer who is standing in front of it.
Read one before sending the seller your next question. The furniture may still surprise you, but it should have to work harder.
